cross_artifact_grounding.text: major: The substantive 'Issues requiring attention' are generic build-risk advice rather than cross-artifact findings — 'State management pattern not explicit', 'Chart rendering complexity ... Implementing this without a charting library is non-trivial', 'Test aggregation functions independently first' would fit any dashboard spec/task pair unchanged; none cites a spec section that disagrees with a task.

minor: Seven of eleven findings rows clear the pair in blanket terms without naming what was checked — 'No internal contradictions detected' (row 1), 'All navigation flows from spec covered' (row 8), 'No deviations expected' (row 9) — so the clearances are unverifiable against the artifacts.

defect_detection.text: blocking: Certifies 'Data model alignment ✅ Clear ... Aggregation logic (Parts & Costs roll-up from WO line items) explicitly assigned to Task 6' when the numbers do not roll up at all. The 15 work orders total $12,840; the Parts & Costs Total column sums to $14,247; the subtotal row claims 'Total: $18,947 | Labor: $6,620 | Parts: $12,327' while its own columns sum to $14,247 / $6,020 / $10,227. Per vehicle: TRK-2026-0184's three WOs (0515 $245, 0512 $180, 0500 $120) = $545 but the cost table says $1,245; BX-2024-0512 = $1,020 vs $1,950; CG-2023-1047 = $840 vs $2,340; TR-2022-0091 = $85 vs $580. This is the brief's one explicit arithmetic requirement ('Parts & Costs totals must sum from work order line items') and the report launders it as clear.

blocking: Misses that the Work Orders dataset carries no shop assignment. The spec promises '15 work orders across 3 shops (5 per shop)' and shop tabs where 'individual shop shows 5', but the WO table columns are [WO #, Vehicle Unit, Task, Assigned Tech, Status, Days in Queue, Priority, Cost] — no shop — and Task 4 writes the gap out loud as '[... shop filter changes which 5 are shown ...]'. The report instead states 'Spec and tasks are mutually consistent ... No internal contradictions detected'. It also breaks the brief's 'moving it between Work Orders queues'.

major: Misses that Vehicle Detail's Work Order History cites WO-2026-0498, WO-2026-0477 and WO-2026-0450 — none of which exist in the 15-row Work Orders dataset — while omitting WO-2026-0500 (Tire Rotation, TRK-2026-0184) which does, and renames WO-2026-0515 from 'Engine Oil Change' to 'Oil Change + Filter Replacement'.

major: Misses that Task 3 hardcodes detail content for TRK-2026-0184 only (header VIN/mileage, 6 checklist rows, 3 shop notes, 5 WOs), while the brief and spec require '#/vehicle/:id' to render 'the clicked vehicle's' data for all 12 vehicles — yet the report rates 'UX flow completeness ✅ Clear'.
minor: Misses the Settings section's 'Total Vehicles: 52' contradicting the data model's 'Vehicle (seed 12 instances)' and the 12-row Vehicles table.

minor: Misses the unmapped '[Logout]' nav item introduced by Task 1 ('Nav items (6 total): Vehicles, Work Orders, Inspections, Parts & Costs, Settings, [Logout]'), which appears in no spec page or navigation flow, while rating 'Scope creep ✅ Clear' and 'Unmapped tasks ✅ Clear'.

minor: Misses the clarifications.md answer scoping the MVP to 'Vehicles (list with filters/search) — fully functional'; both spec and tasks build all six pages fully and neither artifact records the override.

verdict_coherence.text: minor: Suggested next actions restates the verdict twice instead of acting — item 2 'Proceed with caution' and item 4 'Proceed — Spec is ready. Task list is actionable.' are the same recommendation and neither is an action.

minor: Findings row 1 says 'No internal contradictions detected' while Issues 4 and 5 record two places where the tasks unilaterally resolve something the spec leaves open ('[Advance Status] UX pattern task-inferred', '[Flag for Parts] workflow clarity'); the row should read ⚠️ rather than ✅.

rationale: Structure and tone are strong and the report does name Task numbers, pages and entities, so it reads as grounded — but the grounding is thin where it matters: the actionable issues are generic build-risk advice (state management, SVG complexity) rather than spec-vs-task disagreements. Detection is where it fails outright. Two blocking misses: the Parts & Costs figures do not sum from the work orders at any level (per-vehicle, column totals, or the subtotal row), which is the brief's single explicit arithmetic requirement and is affirmatively certified '✅ Clear'; and the work order dataset has no shop field despite shop tabs promising 'individual shop shows 5', a gap Task 4 itself flags in a placeholder line. Two further major misses (phantom work orders in the Vehicle Detail history; detail data hardcoded for one of twelve vehicles) plus smaller ones (52 vs 12 vehicles, unmapped Logout nav item, ignored clarification scoping). A gate that returns 'READY WITH CAUTION' on this pair passes a plan whose central numbers do not reconcile. Verdict coherence is largely intact — issues, risks and next actions do follow from the table it wrote — which is precisely the problem: the table is internally consistent and externally wrong.
strengths: Findings are anchored to this row's artifacts by number and name — 'Task 6 (KPI aggregation + SVG chart complexity), Task 3 (state transitions + cross-page sync), Task 8', 'Task 1 (shell) → foundation; Tasks 2–7 → pages', and the entity list 'Vehicle, WorkOrder, Inspection, ServiceChecklistItem, PartsLineItem, Shop, NotificationRule'.

Correctly catches the responsive-design gap: the spec's 'Prototype targets desktop (1024px+) ... sidebar collapses to icon-only on tablet (<834px)' is assigned to no task, and the report flags it in both the findings table (row 2) and Issue 2.

Correctly identifies two genuine spec-silent decisions the tasks resolve unilaterally — the [Advance Status] dropdown pattern and the [Flag for Parts] line-item assumption — and asks for confirmation rather than asserting a defect.
Issues, risk register and next actions trace back to the findings table, and the risk register names concrete mitigations per task rather than boilerplate.

TRK-2026-0184's three WOs = $545 vs $1,245 listed. This is the brief's one explicit arithmetic requirement.
